Let \(t=\alpha/2\). From \(3\alpha+2\beta=180^\circ\),
\[
\beta=90^\circ-\frac{3\alpha}{2}=90^\circ-3t,
\]
so
\[
\sin\beta=\cos 3t.
\]
The Law of Sines gives
\[
\frac{2}{\sin\alpha}=\frac{3}{\sin\beta}
\Rightarrow \sin\beta=\frac32\sin\alpha.
\]
Thus
\[
\cos 3t=\frac32\sin 2t=3\sin t\cos t.
\]
Also \(\cos 3t=\cos t(4\cos^2 t-3)\), so
\[
4\cos^2 t-3=3\sin t.
\]
Let \(s=\sin t\). Then
\[
4(1-s^2)-3=3s
\Rightarrow 4s^2+3s-1=0
\Rightarrow s=\frac14.
\]
Hence
\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{\sqrt{15}}8,\quad \cos\alpha=\frac78,
\]
and
\[
\sin\beta=\frac{3\sqrt{15}}{16},\quad \cos\beta=\frac{11}{16}.
\]
Now
\[
\sin\gamma=\sin(\alpha+\beta)
=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta
=\frac{\sqrt{15}}8\cdot\frac{11}{16}+\frac78\cdot\frac{3\sqrt{15}}{16}
=\frac{\sqrt{15}}4.
\]
Therefore
\[
c=\frac{2\sin\gamma}{\sin\alpha}
=\frac{2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{15}}4}{\frac{\sqrt{15}}8}
=4.
\]

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
